result.text:
Google Play's new Android memory thresholds land in February 2027, and the RSS + swap part is easy to get wrong.

The metric is dynamic memory = anonymous RSS + swap. File-backed pages are excluded, so Android discarding library code won't lower it, and swapping to zRAM won't make it look like you freed anything.

A few things to watch:

→ Java heap isn't the whole process. On Android 8+, bitmap pixel data lives in native memory
→ RSS counts shared pages in full, PSS splits them across processes. Example: 90 MB private + 30 MB shared with 2 other apps = 120 MB RSS, but 100 MB PSS
→ PSS can shift when other processes start or stop sharing pages

Quick example: 200 MB anonymous memory, 60 MB moves to swap. RSS drops to 140 MB, dynamic memory stays at 200 MB.

The p90 thresholds (apps, not games):

→ 4 GB tier: 2 GB foreground | 1 GB background
→ 8 GB tier: 2.25 GB foreground | 1.5 GB background
→ 16 GB tier: 4.25 GB foreground | 2 GB background

So 1.5 GB in the 4 GB tier is fine in the foreground but over the limit in the background. Mixing both states into one number hides that.

Play uses aggregated p90 over 28 days, so one heavy session doesn't say much on its own.

This blog from @measure_sh walks through all of it, and shows how to flag high-memory sessions (at 75% of target) and tie them back to session replays 👇
https://t.co/acWy44omi8
